title: Sprint 1, task 2: One clean product list
where: Every answer AskMate gives comes from this list. A wrong price here is a wrong price for every customer.
next: Go back to the portal. Your checks are running.

steps.title: Customers ask by product code
steps.body:
Shop staff and plumbers ask by the code printed in HomeShine's catalogue, like OPC 109. Today AskMate says every price is ₹0, finds some products twice, and cannot find others at all.
Do this. Click the button. Each red row shows what a customer asked, what they wanted, and what AskMate said.

steps.title: Look at the messy list
steps.body:
Open data/products_raw.csv. It came out of the shop's old billing software. Look for these:
1. Prices written five ways: ₹ 11,500, Rs. 9900/-, 12400, ₹13,200.00 and Rs 13750.
2. Codes written many ways: opc-180, OPC186, OPC 123 , Opc 122.
3. One empty row, and one product listed twice.
This is normal. Real data is always messy, and cleaning it is a real job called data engineering. You did it for the canteen in Mission 3.

steps.title: Predict first
steps.body:
What does Python do with this?
int("11,500")
steps.explain: int() only understands digits. The comma, the rupee sign and /- must be removed first.

steps.title: Clean the prices
steps.body: The problem. AskMate says every price is ₹0, because int() cannot read ₹ 11,500.
hints: Look at the table. Which bits of text stop int() from working?
Remove each unwanted bit with replace(): the rupee sign, Rs., Rs, /- and the comma. For .00 at the end, int(float(text)) works.
Nearly there:  for junk in ["₹", "Rs.", "Rs", "/-", ","]:  then  text = text.replace(junk, ____)  , then  return int(float(text.strip()))

answer.why: The loop takes each unwanted bit in turn and replaces it with nothing. Rs. comes before Rs, so the dot goes too. float() reads 13200.00, and int() then drops the .00 to give 13200.

steps.well_done: Every price is a real number now.
steps.ask: Make clean_price turn any way a price is written into a whole number of rupees.
steps.gets: a price as text from the file, like "₹ 11,500", "Rs. 9900/-" or "₹13,200.00"
approach: Look at the Try it table. Every price has extra bits around its digits: ₹, Rs., Rs, /- and commas.
Remove each extra bit with text = text.replace(bit, ""). A loop over a list of the bits saves typing. Put Rs. before Rs in the list, so the dot goes too.
Some prices end in .00. float() can read that, and int() then drops the decimals.
steps.where: catalogue.py, the function clean_price. Replace the two lines inside it. Leave tidy and the rest alone.
steps.done: every row of the Try it table is green.

steps.title: Clean the product codes
steps.body: The problem. The list writes codes many ways, and so do customers. opc-180 never equals OPC 180.
hints: Look at the table. Make every code look the same first: same case, no dash, no spaces. Then put one space back.
upper() and replace() make OPC180 out of all of them. The letters are the start of it: text.rstrip("0123456789") gives them.
Nearly there:  text = text.upper().replace("-", "").replace(" ", "")  ,  letters = text.rstrip("0123456789")  , then  return (letters + " " + text[len(____):]).strip()

answer.why: First every code is made the same: capitals, no dash, no spaces, so all of them become OPC180. rstrip removes the digits from the end, which leaves just the letters. The digits are what comes after the letters. Then one space goes between them.

steps.well_done: Every code is written one way now.
steps.ask: Make clean_code write every product code the same way: capital letters, one space, then the number.
steps.gets: a code as people type it: "opc-180", "OPC180" or " OPC 180 "
approach: First make every version look the same: capital letters with upper(), then remove the dash and the spaces. All of them become OPC180.
Find the letters at the start: letters = text.rstrip("0123456789") removes the digits from the end.
The digits are what comes after the letters: text[len(letters):].
Return the letters, one space, and the digits. strip() at the end keeps an empty code empty.
steps.where: catalogue.py, the function clean_code. AskMate cleans the codes customers type with this same function.
steps.done: every row of the Try it table is green.

steps.title: Skip empty and repeated rows
steps.body: The problem. Ask for OPC 109 and AskMate asks "Did you mean Amaze or Amaze?": the list has that product twice. It also reads the empty row as a product.
hints: You need to remember which codes you have already added. Which kind of collection is good at answering "have I seen this before?"
Make an empty list and an empty set. Loop over the rows: skip an empty code, skip a code already in the set, otherwise add the product to the list and its code to the set.

Nearly there: inside the loop,  if not row["code"].strip(): continue  ,  product = product_from(row)  ,  if product["code"] in seen: ____  , then  seen.add(product["code"])  and  products.append(product)

answer.code:
def load_catalogue(path=RAW):
    """Every product in the file, cleaned."""
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(f))
    products, seen = [], set()
    for row in rows:
        if not row["code"].strip():
            continue
        product = product_from(row)
        if product["code"] in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(product["code"])
        products.append(product)
    return products
answer.why: A set answers "have I seen this code?" instantly. continue jumps to the next row, so an empty row or a repeat is never added. The code is checked after cleaning, so OPC 109 and opc-109 count as the same product.

steps.well_done: One clean list: 35 products, each once, each with its real price.
steps.ask: Make load_catalogue skip empty rows, and skip a product it has already added.
steps.gets: the 37 rows of data/products_raw.csv, with one empty row and one repeated row
steps.gives: a list of 35 clean products, each one once
approach: Before the loop, make an empty list for the products and an empty set for the codes you have seen.
Go through the rows one by one. If the row's code is empty, skip the row with continue.
Turn the row into a product with product_from(row). If its code is already in your set, skip it too.
Otherwise add its code to the set and the product to the list. After the loop, return the list.
steps.where: catalogue.py, the function load_catalogue. Keep its first lines, which read the file.
